prompt: This page is cited in drug-encyclopedia entries on synthetic cathinones, for these substances: 2-MMC. Report from the page, exactly as printed (numbers digit by digit, names in the page's own spelling and punctuation, lists complete and in page order): (1) chemical identifiers and names for each of these substances: every name used (INN, systematic, IUPAC or chemical name, other names, synonyms, abbreviations and code names), CAS number(s), molecular formula, molecular weight or molar mass, ATC code, and schedule or control status; (2) forms and products: physical forms, appearance, formulations, product types, product or brand names, packaging, and any seizure or drug-checking findings described (briefly, keeping key terms in the page's wording). Say 'not given' for anything the page does not contain. Do not add anything that is not on the page, and do not quote any passage longer than 15 words.
answer:
**(1) Chemical identifiers and names**

- **Common names:** 2-MMC; 2-Methylmethcathinone
- **Systematic (IUPAC) name:** 2-(Methylamino)-1-(2-methylphenyl)propan-1-one; (RS)-2-(methylamino)-1-(2-methylphenyl)propan-1-one
- **Other chemical names:** 1-(2-Methylphenyl)-2-(methylamino)propane-1-one; 2-(Methylamino)-1-(2-methylphenyl)-1-propanone; 2-(Methylamino)-1-(o-tolyl)propan-1-one
- **Other names:** 2-Methyl-methcathinone; 2-Me-methcathinone; 2-Methyl-N-methylcathinone; 2-Me-MCAT; 2-Methyl MC; Ortomephedrone; Orthomephedrone; 2-Mephedrone
- **EUDA framework name:** 2-Me-MC
- **INN:** not given
- **CAS numbers:** 1246911-71-6 (base); 1246815-51-9 (hydrochloride salt); 2277338-19-7 (R-isomer); 2111020-66-5 (S-isomer)
- **Molecular formula:** C11H15NO
- **Molecular mass:** 177.24
- **ATC code:** not given
- **Schedule/control status:**
  - Not listed in a UN schedule; not under assessment or previously assessed within the UN system (per WHO, March 2025).
  - Subject to restrictive measures in 21 Member States, Türkiye and Norway. Several cite a generic cathinone definition or classify it as an isomer of 4-MMC.
  - Not subject to restrictive measures in six Member States: Bulgaria, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Romania, Slovakia and Spain. Romania reported it is in the process of being controlled.
  - Controlled in China since October 2015; the available information suggests it is not controlled in India.
  - Not an active substance in any medicinal product for human or veterinary use in Europe, based on available information (incomplete for national-level human medicines).

**(2) Forms and products**

- **Physical form:** The hydrochloride salt is described as a crystalline solid. Seized and collected material was mostly powder; tablets, capsules and liquids were reported to a lesser extent.
- **Appearance:** When reported, powders were typically described as white or off-white powders or crystals.
- **Formulations:** not given
- **Product types:** Sold as a substance in its own right and mis-sold as other drugs, particularly 3-MMC. Also reported as mis-sold as 4-MMC and 3-CMC. Pills containing 2-MMC were reported sold as 3-MMC, 4-MMC or 3-CMC (Switzerland).
- **Product or brand names:** not given
- **Packaging:** not given
- **Seizure findings:**
  - 2,314 powder cases (2013–2024) were reported by law enforcement; 2,196 reported weight, totalling 45,832 kg.
  - Most recent cases (2022 onward) accounted for 99.7% of total quantity.
  - 2-MMC was the only substance reported in 90.1% of cases; in 8.2% it was found with other substances, including 2-CMC and 3-CMC.
  - Notable seizures: 74.63 g from a house search in Slovenia (December 2024); a 500 g pure powder seizure in Switzerland.
- **Drug-checking findings:**
  - 1,902 collected samples (2013–2024), with 99.9% since 2022.
  - In 97.0% of powder samples, 2-MMC was the only substance reported.
  - In about 78.8% of cases, 2-MMC was mis-sold as 3-MMC.
  - Quantified samples from Slovenia: mean 85% 2-MMC HCl (2023, n=9) and 94% (2024, n=21).
  - Purity of seized powders was not reported.
